flattened_group_value.why: A group with flatten: true has its inputs' values beside its own, under their own names, as ACTIVATE runs it, so a value at the group's key, given for the run or written in a list's default row, isn't its inputs'. It is kept as it is, as ACTIVATE keeps it, as a secret if the group has a password among its inputs, and what reads inputs.<group> reads it; if the group is ignored, it is dropped with the group's inputs.
fix: Give the group's inputs their values by their own names, beside the group's, or remove the value.

flattened_name_taken.why: A group with flatten: true has its inputs' values beside its own, under their own names, so each of them needs a name that no other input whose value is there has, the group's own among them. ACTIVATE fills such a value from both definitions, in the order the file writes them, which the workflow's meaning shouldn't depend on, so Meridian refuses it, where ACTIVATE runs it.
fix: Rename one of the inputs, or remove the group's flatten: true.

input_flag_unsplit.why: -input sets one input, as path=value. Without an =, there is no path, and the problem doesn't repeat what was given, which can be a password.
fix: Write it as path=value, as -input nodes=8.

input_flag_wrong_type.why: -input converts its value by the type of the input it sets, as ACTIVATE's pw workflows run --input does: a boolean input takes true or false, exactly; a number input a JSON number, so 007, 0x10, +1, .5 and 1. aren't one, nor is a number too large for 64 bits; and a header takes no value. The problem doesn't repeat the value, which can be a password.
fix: Give the input a value of its type, as -input debug=false or -input nodes=8.

input_flag_not_json.why: A list, a multi-dropdown, a repeated wizard step, a group, a wizard step, a compute target, and a compute-clusters, compute-resources or bucket input with multi: true take a structure, which -input reads as JSON, as ACTIVATE's pw workflows run --input does. The problem says where the JSON goes wrong, by byte, and doesn't repeat the value, which can hold a password.
fix: Write the value as JSON, quoted for the shell, as -input 'files=["a.txt"]'.

input_flag_wrong_shape.why: -input reads a structure's value as JSON, which must be the shape its input takes, as ACTIVATE's pw workflows run --input reads it: an array for a list, a multi-dropdown, a repeated wizard step and a multi input, and an object for a group, a wizard step and a compute target.
fix: Write the value as the JSON its input takes: an array, in square brackets, or an object, in braces.

input_flag_path_not_settable.why: A path is an input's name, or a group's name and its input's, as group.name, as ACTIVATE's pw workflows run --input reads one. A wizard step that flattens, as one does unless $meta.wizard.flatten is false, and a group with flatten: true put their inputs beside them, so those inputs are set by their own names; a list, or a repeated wizard step, is set whole, as JSON; and an input that holds no inputs has none to set.
fix: Name the input by its own name, or set the list whole, as JSON.

fenced.why: The coordinator checks every write against the attempt's fencing number, so that an attempt another of its job has superseded, as when its lease lapsed and the job ran again, can't change what the run records. A report from an attempt that has completed, other than one repeated as it was, is refused the same way. The worker stops its job's steps, as a cancellation does, and exits.
fix: Nothing to fix: the coordinator decides how the attempt ended, and whether the job runs again.

out_of_order.why: A worker numbers its events and sends a log's bytes from an offset, so that a report repeated after a dropped connection is stored once, and in order. This one skipped some, started past the end of the log or after it had ended, or ended the attempt before the coordinator had every event it counts. The worker sends again from where the coordinator expects.
fix: Nothing to fix: the worker sends again from where the coordinator expects.

plan_too_new.why: A run's plan, and the worker API's bodies, are versioned, and a worker says the newest version it reads as it claims an attempt. The coordinator refuses one that doesn't read the run's, before it sends anything of the run, so that no worker runs a job with a part it doesn't understand. The worker exits, and the attempt, which failed before its first step, is placed again.
fix: Start workers of the same release of Meridian as the coordinator.

fips_not_enforced.why: Meridian is built with Go's validated FIPS 140-3 cryptographic module, and runs only with GODEBUG's fips140=only, which makes the use of an algorithm the module doesn't approve an error. The binary makes fips140=only its default, but the GODEBUG environment variable overrides a default, and a worker can be started by hand or over SSH with any environment. So every meridian command, the worker above all, refuses to run without it, rather than run with weaker cryptography.
fix: Remove fips140 from GODEBUG, or set it to fips140=only, and run the command again.
In a program that runs Meridian's worker itself (worker.Run), make fips140=only its default: add godebug fips140=only to its go.mod, or //go:debug fips140=only to its main package.

fips_module_not_validated.why: Go's FIPS 140-3 module is validated in the frozen versions that GOFIPS140 names as it builds a program, such as certified. A build without GOFIPS140 compiles the module from Go's source, as the version latest, which isn't the validated module, whatever mode it runs in. Meridian refuses to run with it, rather than run with cryptography that isn't validated.
fix: Build meridian with GOFIPS140=certified: with make build in its repository, with GOFIPS140=certified go install github.com/parallelworks/meridian/cmd/meridian@ and the version, or once for every build with go env -w GOFIPS140=certified.

isolation_not_built.why: A member names how it isolates the jobs placed on it: a container runtime, such as podman, docker or apptainer, or host, which runs a job's steps on the host, as you. A member that names none isolates them in a rootless container. The local backend runs jobs on the host only, today, and Meridian never runs a job with weaker isolation than its member names, so placement leaves the member out, and places the job on another member of its group if there is one.
fix: Name host isolation for the member in groups.yaml, if running its jobs' steps on the host, as you, is what you want.

resources_exceed_member.why: A member offers the resources it declares in groups.yaml or, for one of the local backend that declares none, the host's CPUs and memory, and no GPU unless it declares some. A job whose resources: asks for more than that can never run there, so placement leaves the member out, and places the job on another member of its group if one offers enough.
fix: Ask for less in the job's resources:, declare what the member offers in groups.yaml, or run the job in a group with a member that offers enough.

backend_not_built.why: A member names the backend that starts workers on it: local, ssh, kubernetes, slurm or pbs. This release of Meridian has only the local backend, so placement leaves a member of another backend out, and places the job on another member of its group if there is one.
fix: Run the job in a group with a member of the local backend, until a release has the member's backend.

worker_binary_unsafe.why: The local backend starts each worker from the meridian binary that places it, and the worker holds the attempt's credential once it runs. So the binary must be a regular file of yours or root's that no other user can change, nor any directory on the way to it: otherwise another user could replace it with a program that reads what the worker is given. The code is the problem with it, and its page says why.
fix: Fix what the code's page says, for the binary the message names, or install meridian where only you or root can change it, such as /usr/local/bin.
